sentences.text:
*** *
 Mr. A. R. Patil, Addl. G.P. for the Appellant.
None for the Respondent

** * *
 Coram : M. M. Sathaye, J
 Dated : 10th July, 2025
 P.C.:
1. Heard learned Agp for the Appellant/State.
None for the Respondent.

2.  This is an appeal by the State under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act (for short 'the said Act') challenging the Judgment and Award dated 08/08/2000 passed in Land Acquisition Reference (LAR) No. 49 of 1994 by the Civil Judge, Senior Division, Rajnagiri.
3.
Few facts necessary for disposal of the appeal are as under.
The land of the Respondent at mouje Kond was compulsorily acquired for Shil- Irrigation Project.
The concerned Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) passed an award granting compensation of Rs.5,04,224/- in which Respondent had 1/6th share amounting to Rs. 84,037/- only.

The Respondent/Claimant filed above Reference under Section 18 of the said The State Of Maharashtra vs Suhas Narsinha Mulye on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173196721/
1 28.FA.733.2008 C.doc Act, seeking enhancement.

entities.text: State Of Maharashtra vs Suhas Narsinha Mulye
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After considering the evidence on record, the Reference Court has allowed the reference thereby granting enhancement of meager Rs.34,641/-
alongwith interest.
4. The learned Addl. GP has argued the Appeal as per memo of Appeal.
It is contended that the enhancement could not have been granted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It is fairly conceded that the amount under the award passed by SLAO is not challenged.
5. I have carefully considered the impugned judgment and order.
The detailed reasons given by the Reference Court on the basis of which, the enhancement is granted, are well founded.

After going through the evidence on record such as sale instances, proximity with acquired land, the nature of trees and fruits in the subject matter land and its annual yield, the Reference Court has arrived at a conclusion that the Respondent-Claimant is entitled to enhancement of Rs.34,641/- with interest and 30% solatium and 12% additional component.
Therefore it is clear that the amount of enhancement granted is meager / paltry, which is sought to be challenged by the State, when the amount of compensation itself was also meager / paltry.

6. Facts of this case are more or less similar to a group of First Appeals disposed of by another Single Bench of this Court with lead First Appeal No. 208 of 1992 along with others under Order dated 03.04.2017 (Coram : M.S. Sonak, J.).
I am completely in agreement with the view taken by my brother Judge in the said Order that such appeals challenging meager amounts of compensation or enhancement have no merit.

It has to be noted that state compulsorily acquires lands of the citizens like Respondent/Claimant and despite the compensation amount being so paltry / meagre, the State carries the matters in appeal.

In many cases, it is found that on account of pendency 28.FA.733.2008 C.doc of the Appeal (primarily because no steps are taken by the State to effect service or bring legal heirs on record or reasons alike), the Respondent/Claimant remains deprived of even meagre amounts of compensation awarded to them.
It is also sadly noted that the State Government in such Appeals, spends amounts on Court fees, typing and other filing expenses and legal fees from the State exchequer.
7. Considering the meager amount of enhancement under challenge, that too granted under a well reasoned impugned judgment, I do not find myself persuaded to take any different view.
There is no merit in Appeal.
8. Hence the Appeal is dismissed.
No order as to costs.

In view of the dismissal of Appeal, the Respondent/Claimant or his legal heirs as the case may be, is/are at liberty to withdraw the amount of compensation, if deposited by the State in the Reference Court along with accrued interest, if not already withdrawn.
Needless to mention that the impugned order becomes executable.
9. All concerned to act on duly authenticated or digitally signed copy of this order.

(M. M. SATHAYE, J.)
